prompt_text: Where should I stay in Branson Missouri, an Airbnb or a hotel, and which specific places are best?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: it depends on what you want to do in Branson.

Quick guidance
- Stay in a hotel if you want convenience, predictable service, on-site amenities (pool/restaurant/front desk), easy late check-ins, and fewer hassles with rules/cleanup. Good for couples, older travelers, or short stays focused on shows.
- Stay in an Airbnb (condo, lakefront cabin, or whole house) if you want more space, a kitchen, a better price for groups/families, privacy, or a “home base” vibe—especially if you plan to cook, stay longer, or want a lake cabin experience.

Where to stay (areas + when to pick them)
- 76 Country Boulevard (“The Strip”) — Best if you’re coming for the theater shows, attractions, and quick access to restaurants. Lots of hotels, chain motels, and short-term rentals within walking distance of show venues.
- Branson Landing / Downtown — Good for lakefront dining, shopping, the boardwalk, and evening strolls. Condos and the Hilton Promenade are right on the Landing.
- Table Rock Lake / Big Cedar Lodge / Ridgedale — Best if you want a lakeside/resort experience, boating, hiking, golf, and a more upscale/relaxed stay.
- Near Silver Dollar City / Branson West — Best if the theme park is your main focus (shorter drive to the park).
- Hollister / South Branson — Quieter, often more residential or cabin-style rentals for families/groups.

Specific places I’d recommend to consider
Hotels / resorts
- Chateau on the Lake Resort Spa & Convention Center — Upscale lakeside resort with spa and great views; good for a romantic or pampered stay.
- Big Cedar Lodge (near Ridgedale) — Rustic-luxury cabins and resort amenities; excellent if you want outdoor activities and a high-end cabin feel.
- Hilton Promenade at Branson Landing — Convenient, modern option right on the Landing (good balance of comfort and location for shopping/dining).
- The Keeter Center at College of the Ozarks — Well-regarded, unique (students work on campus); quieter and family-friendly with a different kind of atmosphere.
- Chain hotels along Hwy 76 (Hampton Inn, Fairfield/Marriott, Best Western, etc.) — Reliable, budget-to-midrange options near the theaters.

Airbnb / vacation-rental types to look for
- Branson Landing condos — Walkable to shops/restaurants and often newer/clean with lake access.
- Table Rock Lake cabins / lakefront houses — For boating, sunsets, and big family stays (look for private dock access if you want to boat).
- Large 4–6+ bedroom houses near the Strip — Practical and often cheaper per person for groups going to multiple shows.
- Luxury cabins near Big Cedar or in the Ozarks — If you want cabins with hot tubs, fire pits, and mountain views.

Booking tips
- Book far in advance for high season (summer) and holiday events (Ozark Mountain Christmas) — hotels and rentals fill early.
- For Airbnbs, read recent reviews, confirm AC (Branson summers are hot), parking, and whether the listing has easy check-in and clear cancellation terms. Watch for high cleaning/service fees.
- If you plan lots of shows, staying on/near 76 saves drive time and parking hassles. If you plan lake activities, stay at or near Table Rock Lake.
- For families/groups, prioritize a kitchen, laundry, and parking space.
- If you need wheelchair access or late check-in, hotels usually make that easier.

If you tell me:
- your travel dates, budget, group size, and main priorities (shows vs lake vs theme park vs relaxation), I’ll give 3 tailored picks (one hotel, one Airbnb type, and one splurge) and link-style suggestions for each.
